essay_text: Education in Malawi is organized along bureaucratic lines that mirror the broader formal organisational structures described by sociologists. First, employment based on technical qualifications ensures that teachers are hired based on professional training and competence rather than personal connections, thus maintaining educational quality. Second, hierarchical delegation of power runs from the Head Teacher through deputy heads, section heads, subject heads, subject teachers, prefects and the student body, ensuring smooth delegation when key personnel are absent. Third, rules and regulations govern student and staff conduct including uniform requirements, punctuality, and prohibition of romantic relationships, maintaining order and a conducive learning environment. Fourth, impartiality ensures positions are assigned through formal procedures without nepotism or inheritance. Fifth, clear-cut division of labour assigns specific roles to specialists whose repeated performance leads to mastery. Together these characteristics make Malawian secondary schools function efficiently as formal organisations (Ballantine et al, 2017).
